assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology to incretin-based therapy is one of the clearest bench-to-bedside arcs of the era: identification of the active peptide forms, insulinotropic and satiety actions, and long-acting agonists that transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care with large outcome trials showing cardiometabolic benefit. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Credit is the hard part. Holst (physiology of GLP-1 and incretin effect) and Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptide biology, GLP-2, translational program) are central; Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form and synthesis is a decisive but contested contribution; Knudsen's medicinal-chemistry work enabled liraglutide and semaglutide but is pharmaceutical development. I propose the physiology-centred trio.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of replication, approved drugs, outcome trials, and mechanistic understanding of gut-brain and islet action. Recognition is timely given broad clinical adoption.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Habener-group work, Mojsov, Holst and Drucker is disputed and the longlist does not include all possible contributors.
Whether drug development (Knudsen) should be recognised alongside physiology is unresolved.
Long-term safety and durability of effects are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signalling: ER stress sensed by IRE1, with HAC1/XBP1 splicing and downstream transcriptional programs. Conceptually foundational for proteostasis, secretory physiology, and disease including diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Clean two-person configuration: Walter (IRE1, unconventional mRNA splicing, ISRIB-era follow-up) and Mori (UPR element and HAC1/IRE1 signalling) were decisive and independent. Other contributors such as Ron, Kaufman and Schekman-era secretory pathway work exist but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, extensively confirmed from yeast to mammals for 30 years. Timing is fine; therapeutic translation is still developing but is not needed for basic-science prize.
uncertainties: Other pioneers of ER stress signalling (PERK, ATF6 branches) are outside the credited names, which may leave the configuration open to challenge.
Clinical translation remains early.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics created a general method for causal control of defined cell types with light, from the discovery of channelrhodopsin photocurrents to its neuronal deployment. It has changed experimental neuroscience and physiology and enabled circuit-level causal inference; early clinical uses (vision restoration) are emerging.
assessment.attribution: Strongest scientific core is channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) plus neuronal implementation and broad toolkit development (Deisseroth, Boyden, Miesenboeck's earlier genetic approach). With six credited names, a three-person cap forces hard choices; I favour Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth but acknowledge the case for Boyden and Bamberg.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research tool with thousands of independent applications; clinical impact is still limited, so the case rests on research transformation.
uncertainties: Credit is divided between molecular discovery and neuroscience implementation, and the three-laureate limit makes any configuration contestable.
Early clinical translation is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells, especially CD19 CAR-T, produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. Impact on oncology and cell engineering is large and increasingly extends to autoimmune disease.
assessment.attribution: June (CD28/4-1BB CAR design and first durable clinical responses) and Sadelain (CD28 co-stimulated CARs, preclinical foundations) are central; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T cell trials. Other contributors such as Eshhar and Kuwana's chimeric receptor concept, and Brentjens, lie outside the list; this is a sensitive configuration.
assessment.maturity: Approved products for a decade with real-world data; durability, solid-tumour limits and toxicity are still being worked out, but recognition is plausible now.
uncertainties: Early chimeric-receptor concept originators are not credited, complicating fair attribution.
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and safety issues remain.
Whether Rosenberg or Sadelain should be in the trio is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that increase SMN2 exon 7 inclusion produced nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy and a proof of principle for RNA-targeted drugs. Very clear mechanism-to-medicine link with dramatic clinical effect in infants.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the SMN2 splicing mechanism and the ASO target; Bennett led the antisense chemistry and drug development at Ionis. Two-person configuration is clean, though Hua, Singh and the SMN2 discovery by Lefebvre/Melki (SMN1 gene) are adjacent contributions.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with long-term follow-up; extension to other splice-modifying and ASO therapies supports the generality. Timely, though still relatively young as a prize candidate.
uncertainties: The gene discovery of SMN1 by Lefebvre and Melki is a separate foundation not credited here.
Therapy requires repeated intrathecal dosing and long-term outcomes are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING established a central pathway by which cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity through cGAMP, with implications for antiviral defence, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and senescence. A major conceptual advance with wide influence.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP, the decisive step; Barber discovered STING and its role in DNA sensing. Ishikawa co-discovered STING and Wu and Sun are Chen-lab contributors, so credit is broader than two; I propose Chen and Barber, with Ishikawa a plausible alternative.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed mechanistically, with structural work by others. Therapeutic agonists and antagonists are not yet approved, so the clinical payoff is still pending.
uncertainties: Ishikawa and Barber's overlapping STING discovery complicates credit.
Cyclic dinucleotide sensing in bacteria and structural contributions by others are outside the list.
No approved therapy yet.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Lgr5 stem-cell identification and long-term culture of self-organising intestinal organoids gave a general platform for modelling epithelial tissues, disease and personalised drug testing. Large influence on stem-cell and experimental medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the clear intellectual leader (Lgr5 stem cells and the organoid system); Sato was first author of the key culture papers. Barker and others contributed to the Lgr5 stem-cell identification and are not credited, which weakens a clean allocation.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used, but clinical impact is still emerging, so the case is partly one of future promise.
uncertainties: Recognition of Lgr5 stem cell work by Barker and colleagues is outside the credited names.
Translational value of organoids is not yet established at clinical scale.
Overlap with Wnt signalling prior work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib targeted BCR-ABL kinase in chronic myeloid leukemia and turned a fatal leukemia into a manageable chronic disease, establishing the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Very clear and lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (clinical translation and championing of the trial program) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio. Fundamental BCR-ABL and Philadelphia chromosome discoveries by Rowley, Witte and others are not on the list and have been partly recognised elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with more than two decades of survival data. Possible concern that the prize has been long delayed rather than premature.
uncertainties: Foundational oncogene work (Abl, Philadelphia chromosome) is attributed to others.
Drug-discovery chemistry credit within Novartis (Zimmermann, Buchdunger) is not captured in the list.
